name: Navigator
description: The Navigator OS brand colour palette — a nautical & sky identity themed around the compass, lighthouse, Orion and the North Star.

teal.description: The primary accent colour — interactive elements, focus states, the assistant panel

purple.description: The secondary accent colour — pairs with teal in gradients, the AI/assistant context

gold.description: The North Star accent — notifications, warnings, brand details

navy.description: The navy base — the night-sky ground, window backgrounds, the panel ground

text.description: Primary text on the navy ground — a near-white with a blue cast so it belongs to the night sky rather than sitting on top of it

surface.description: Raised surfaces on the navy ground — text views, entries, tooltips, menus

surface_alt.description: Buttons, header bars, alternating rows — between navy and surface

border.description: Separators and widget borders — visible against navy without competing with the accents

assistant.usage: The active window border, the assistant panel accent (see hyprland/hyprland.conf)

notes: 'colors' are the brand identity and appear in the logo, the wallpaper and the compositor. 'ui' are interface surfaces, derived to sit on the navy ground; they exist because a widget theme needs a foreground, surfaces and borders that a four-colour brand palette does not provide. Keeping them here rather than inventing them inside each theme file is what stops GTK and Qt drifting apart.
Everything in 'ui' except 'text' is a shade of navy. They are literal hexes rather than computed at load time because Qt colour schemes cannot express a formula.

The colour values inside hyprland/hyprland.conf, shell/Theme.qml, theme/gtk/ and theme/qt/ are repeated by hand from this file, and CI verifies that duplication — see .github/workflows/brand-check.yml and the 'Layer 3/4/7' step of build-disk-and-boot-test.yml.
